Islamic Relief Worldwide (IRW) - founded in 1984 and based in Birmingham, UK - is an independent humanitarian and development organization. It supports the world’s most vulnerable people in their fight against poverty & sufferings regardless of race, political affiliation, gender, or belief, and without expecting anything in return. It is a signatory to the Code of Conduct for the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement. 
IRW has a presence in 45 countries across the globe. Some funds of the organization come from individual donations and others from institutional donors such as the DFID, EU, SIDA, CIDA/IDRF, Forum Syd, WFP, UNDP, and ECHO.
Islamic Relief(IR) started working in Bangladesh in 1991 in order to help the distressed survivors of the devastating cyclone by providing emergency relief and supporting communities to rebuild in the wake of that cyclone. Initially, it focused on emergency relief & disaster preparedness activities. Later on, it expanded its programs on both humanitarian and development challenges. Now it works in an integrated manner combining emergency humanitarian assistance, short-term work opportunity, shelter support, awareness & training on different DRR, climate change, development, health & hygiene and social issues, cash grant, IGA means, health & nutrition, safe water & sanitation, education, advocacy and linkage with different service providers. As a registered charity, IR is open and transparent; it continually assesses its work and operational methods to improve impact and effectiveness. 
Islamic Relief values and commitment to safeguarding: IRB is committed to preventing any type of unwanted behavior at work including sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity, and financial misconduct; and committed to promoting the welfare of children, young people, adults, and beneficiaries with whom IRB engages. IRB expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We place a high priority on ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us. All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records checks. IRW also participates in the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme.
In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment.

It supports the world’s most vulnerable people in their fight against poverty & sufferings regardless of race, political affiliation, gender, or belief, and without expecting anything in return. It is a signatory to the Code of Conduct for the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement. 
IRW has a presence in 45 countries across the globe. Some funds of the organization come from individual donations and others from institutional donors such as the DFID, EU, SIDA, CIDA/IDRF, Forum Syd, WFP, UNDP, and ECHO.
Islamic Relief(IR) started working in Bangladesh in 1991 in order to help the distressed survivors of the devastating cyclone by providing emergency relief and supporting communities to rebuild in the wake of that cyclone. Initially, it focused on emergency relief & disaster preparedness activities. Later on, it expanded its programs on both humanitarian and development challenges. Now it works in an integrated manner combining emergency humanitarian assistance, short-term work opportunity, shelter support, awareness & training on different DRR, climate change, development, health & hygiene and social issues, cash grant, IGA means, health & nutrition, safe water & sanitation, education, advocacy and linkage with different service providers. As a registered charity, IR is open and transparent; it continually assesses its work and operational methods to improve impact and effectiveness. 
Islamic Relief values and commitment to safeguarding: IRB is committed to preventing any type of unwanted behavior at work including sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity, and financial misconduct; and committed to promoting the welfare of children, young people, adults, and beneficiaries with whom IRB engages. IRB expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We place a high priority on ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us. All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records checks. IRW also participates in the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme.
In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment.

Bangladesh is recognized as one of the country’s most vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) has identified the coastal region as one of the major climate hotspot areas due to increasing salinity intrusion, sea-level rise, cyclones, storm surges, tidal flooding, and coastal erosion. These climate-induced hazards have significantly affected the livelihoods, health, and living conditions of coastal communities. Among the most critical challenges is the scarcity of safe drinking water, as freshwater sources are increasingly becoming saline and unsuitable for human consumption. The experience of HEED Bangladesh indicates that climate-vulnerable coastal communities continue to face severe difficulties in accessing safe and reliable drinking water. Salinity intrusion into both surface and groundwater sources, coupled with the impacts of recurrent cyclones and tidal surges, has substantially reduced the availability of potable water. As a result, people—particularly women and children—are compelled to travel long distances to collect drinking water, exposing them to health risks, economic hardship, and reduced productivity. Limited access to safe drinking water also contributes to waterborne diseases and undermines the resilience of vulnerable households. Under these circumstances, to improve access to safe drinking water and strengthen the climate resilience of vulnerable coastal communities in Dacopeupazila of Khulna districts, HEED Bangladesh will implement the project titled “Access to Safe Drinking Water for the Climate Vulnerable People in Coastal Areas of Bangladesh through Solar-generated Reverse Osmosis Water Treatment Facilities.” The project will be financed by the Adaptation Fund (AF) through Palli Karma-Sahayak Foundation (PKSF) and will be implemented over a period of two years. The specific objectives of the project are: •	Ensure access to safe and climate-resilient drinking water for vulnerable coastal communities through the installation and operation of Reverse Osmosis (RO) water treatment plants. •	Enhance awareness and knowledge of climate-vulnerable communities on safe drinking water, health, hygiene, and climate change adaptation practices. Hence, HEED Bangladesh is seeking qualified candidates for the post of "Technician" to implement the project and provide overall technical support for the successful implementation of the project activities. Job Responsibilities: The Technician acts as the Field Implementation Lead to ensure effective community engagement, smooth implementation of project activities, and achievement of project objectives at the grassroots level. The role focuses on community mobilization, beneficiary identification and support, field-level monitoring, and coordination with local stakeholders. The position serves as the primary field-level bridge between the community, HEED Bangladesh and the Project Focal Person. The Technician works under the direct supervision and technical guidance of the Project Focal Person and is responsible for executing day-to-day field activities in compliance with project guidelines.  The Technician will be responsible for the following duties: •	Facilitate monthly meetings of community groups, ensuring active participation and discussion of climate change challenges, adaptation strategies, and project activities. •	Work with community groups to identify beneficiaries and participants for various project activities, including RO plant installation, water distribution, and livelihood support initiatives. •	Ensure transparent and inclusive selection of beneficiaries, with special attention to vulnerable and marginalized groups, including women and persons with disabilities. •	Supervise and monitor day-to-day field activities to ensure they are implemented according to the approved work plan, timeline, and technical specifications. •	Coordinate with the Technical Officer (Engineering) to support smooth installation, commissioning, and operation of RO plants. •	Support promotional activities for the RO plants to increase water sales and ensure revenue generation for sustainability. •	Promote the adoption of climate-smart practices, water conservation, and sustainable livelihoods within the community. •	Regularly monitor project activities, collect field-level data on community demographics, livelihoods, climate perceptions, and project impacts. •	Prepare regular reports on community engagement activities, awareness campaigns, beneficiary selection processes, and field-level progress. •	Document success stories, lessons learned, and challenges faced during project implementation for knowledge sharing and reporting. •	Assist with data collection and reporting for project monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEAL) activities. •	Submit all field reports to the Technical Officer (Engineering) for review and validation. •	Liaise with the Focal person of the project, Technical Officer (Engineering), and PMU of PKSF to ensure efficient data sharing, reporting, and coordination of activities. •	Conduct on-site training and orientation for water user groups and operators on project objectives, safe water practices, operation and maintenance, and hygiene promotion. •	Ensure all field activities meet environmental and social safeguards. •	Perform any other duties assigned by the Project Focal Person as per instruction from PKSF and PO Management.
